events.title: .NET 11 security changes target the software supply chain
events.summary: Microsoft has shipped .NET 11, a two-year Standard Term Support release spanning C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI and Windows development, with several changes aimed at software supply chain integrity, authentication handling and platform lifecycle. Alongside the release, .NET 8 and .NET 9 have dropped out of support, while .NET 10 remains the long-term support option.
events.why_it_matters: With .NET 8 and .NET 9 now unsupported, applications still running on those runtimes will no longer receive patches, giving defenders a concrete deadline to migrate or accept growing risk. The release's focus on supply chain integrity and authentication handling signals where Microsoft sees its platform's security gaps. Teams planning upgrades should note .NET 10 remains the LTS option for those needing longer support horizons.
